text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The Coalition Party held its congress on saturday and re-elected Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi as chairman.

- The defence ministry held a meeting for students with the defence forces commander and a visit to an infantry battalion on Saturday. It was explained that there will be no massive training of reserve officers in the universities.
- The draft law on customs tariffs is expected to reach parliament early next year.
- Foreign Minister Toomas Ilves expressed his satisfaction with the appointment of new top officials of the U.S. administration as supporters of the Baltic states.
- There are three major potential sources of strikes in Sillamae, Oru and Narva in northeastern Estonia and the reasons are low or late wages.
- The number of Estonians willing to emigrate to Estonia from Russia after the border agreement has been approved is unknown and there have been no applicants so far.
- German navy commander, vice-admiral Hans Rudolf Boehmer, is to visit Estonia on December 9-10. He is to discuss German aid and the disposal of World War II mines in Estonian waters.
- Russian foreign ministry experts are to arrive in Estonia to study the situation of the Russian-speaking population.
- A large Chinese business delegation has offered trade opportunities with China but Estonian businessmen are slow in using them, economy ministry officials said.

- The planning head of U.S. energy firm Duke Energy visited Estonia last week to study investing in the Estonian energy industry after privatisation. This is the second U.S. energy company to express interest in that sector.
- Government, trade unions and employers agreed to raise the minimum wages to 845 kroons per month by February 1997, more than 200 kroons higher than the current level.
